reason: MANE and APPRIS agree on a 1,130-aa protein that adds 94 residues before the signal peptide of the 1,036-aa UniProt canonical. With the extension DeepTMHMM v1 no longer calls a signal peptide: it reads the signal peptide as a second TM helix and puts the N-terminus inside (2 TM, N-in; canonical: SP + 1 TM, N-out). The mouse and cyno models in L2 are also 1,130 aa, so the extension may be translated, but nothing in this audit shows the extended protein reaching the surface. The 1,036-aa reviewed UniProt form has a clean, cleavable signal peptide at residue 1 and the canonical type I topology, which is the form a surface-display library needs. Met95 is a native ATG, so the repair is a 5' trim with no codon edit.
alternative: keep the 1,130-aa MANE / APPRIS form with its 94-residue extension

decided_by: l1-reviewer-package (delegated by Becca 2026-11-12), reconciling l1-proteoform-audit (canonical) and l1-nterm-type3 (Q96KR4-3, #282 f980ce49)
reason: The APPRIS-only reference ENST00000482695 (452 aa, no UniProt isoform) starts at canonical residue 233. It lacks the signal peptide DeepTMHMM v1 calls on the canonical (43 aa) and canonical residues 1-232, so as ordered it has no route to the secretory pathway (v1: no SP, no TM). The 647-aa canonical has its own Ensembl 115 transcript. A new CDS has to be designed for it. Reconciled choice: the UniProt canonical Q96KR4 via ENST00000330198, whose CDS starts ATG and encodes Q96KR4 exactly (the fallback, Q96KR4-3 already built in L2 as l2-p0894, was not needed). Both forms keep the same 43-aa signal peptide (DeepTMHMM v1 SP 1-43, identical N-termini); NetGPI calls both GPI-anchored (canonical omega 620, isoform-3-like forms omega ~656, likelihood 0.461 each); isoform 3 differs only by a 37-aa insertion after residue 403 with no evidence for its function, so the canonical is preferred.
alternative: Q96KR4-3 (l2-p0894, ENST00000420910, 684 aa); keep the 452-aa downstream ENST00000482695 form
